memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water." - Lev 8:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before the robes, before the oil, before the blood — water.

Aaron and his sons are washed. This was not a symbolic sprinkle; it was a full washing, and Moses did it for them. They did not wash themselves.

That order matters. Cleansing comes first. Everything else in the ordination — the garments, the anointing, the sacrifices — is placed on top of men who have been made clean.

It is the same order in the gospel. God saved us, not because of righteous things we had done, but because of his mercy. He saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Tit 3:5). Paul reminds the Corinthians, some of whom had appalling histories: But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified (1 Cor 6:11).

Note the passive voice in both passages. You were washed. Someone did it to you.

Many believers exhaust themselves trying to scrub up before God will accept them. But nobody in Scripture ever cleaned themselves up first. Aaron stood there and let Moses wash him.

If you have been trying to make yourself presentable before coming to God, stop. Come and be washed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trying to clean myself up before approaching God?
2. Do I believe that Christ's cleansing of me is complete?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I cannot make myself clean. Wash me, and let everything else in my life rest on what You have done. Amen.
